alternatives.mechanism: AI‑driven visual pantry scanner where users snap a quick photo of their fridge/shelf; the system extracts ingredient types and estimated expiration dates.
addresses_issues: Reliance on user‑provided pantry data that may be incomplete or inaccurate
Privacy concerns around sharing pantry inventories
tradeoffs: Requires camera permission and on‑device processing which may affect battery
Image recognition can misidentify items, leading to suboptimal suggestions
Some users may feel uncomfortable photographing food
alternatives.novelty_or_difference: Uses on‑device computer vision to auto‑populate pantry data, reducing manual entry.

alternatives.mechanism: Gamified suggestion platform that awards points/badges when users prepare recommended meals and log leftover amounts; points can be exchanged for discounts or community status.
addresses_issues: User willingness to follow suggested meals is uncertain
tradeoffs: Relies on self‑reported waste which may be biased
May attract users motivated by rewards rather than genuine waste reduction
alternatives.novelty_or_difference: Adds a game layer to motivate compliance and generate crowd‑sourced waste data.

alternatives.mechanism: Integration with smart kitchen devices (e.g., RFID‑enabled containers or barcode scanners) that automatically sync ingredient inventories and expiration dates to the app, keeping data local on the device.
addresses_issues: Reliance on user‑provided pantry data that may be incomplete or inaccurate
Privacy concerns around sharing pantry inventories
tradeoffs: Requires users to own compatible smart hardware, increasing cost
Data accuracy depends on correct tagging of items
alternatives.novelty_or_difference: Leverages IoT hardware to capture pantry state without manual entry, enhancing privacy by processing locally.
